hook_text: Debit does not mean bad and credit does not mean good. In accounting, they just mean left and right.
clip_script: One car wash, one owner: a sole trader. She puts in fifty thousand rand of savings: that is capital. Buys a high-pressure washer: an asset, something the business owns. Borrows twenty thousand from the bank: a liability, something it owes. Every car washed brings in a fee: income. Wages, water, soap: expenses. Forty-eight thousand in, twenty-six thousand out: twenty-two thousand profit. She takes six thousand home: drawings, not an expense. Her share of the business is now fifty plus twenty-two minus six: sixty-six thousand rand. That is owner's equity. Now draw a T. Left side, debit. Right side, credit. Remember DEAD: debits increase expenses, assets and drawings. Everything else goes up on the right.
visual_style: A whiteboard car wash with labels popping up on the washer, the bank, the loan and the workers, then a big T-account with DEAD written down the left side.
mood: Confident myth-busting with a clean memory trick.
pacing: Rapid labelling of the car wash, a quick profit sum, then the T and DEAD written slowly.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and classify every item on the corner.
